ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in Figure A, this is an image of an alternating voltage changing with time. In each period, the voltage is constant in the first half period, and in the second half period the voltage changes according to a sinusoidal law. If this alternating current is connected into the circuit shown in Figure B, and the resistance R has a value of 100 Ω, what is the reading of the ideal ammeter?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Figure A is an image of voltage u changing with time t, the vertical axis is marked u/V, and the horizontal axis is marked t/(×10^-2 s). Within one period, from 0 to 1 the voltage is a constant 100 V; from 1 to 2 the voltage starts from 0 and becomes negative in a sinusoidal shape, reaches a minimum of about -50 V, and then returns to 0. Then from 2 to 3 it is again constant at 100 V, and from 3 to 4 it again repeats the negative half-cycle sinusoidal change, so the period is T=2×10^-2 s. In Figure B, the alternating-current power supply is connected into the circuit, the ideal voltmeter is connected in parallel across the two ends of the power supply, the ideal ammeter is connected in series with resistor R, the resistor is labeled R, and the problem gives R=100 Ω. Reasoning: The reading of an alternating-current ammeter is the effective current, so first find the effective voltage. Divide one period according to Figure A: in the first T/2, u=100 V; in the second T/2, it is a negative half-cycle sinusoidal voltage with amplitude 50 V, whose square mean value, like a sine, is 50^2/2. By the definition of effective value: U_eff^2=[100^2·(T/2)+(50^2/2)·(T/2)]/T=5000+625=5625. Therefore U_eff=75 V. The ideal ammeter is connected in series in the resistor branch, and the reading is the effective current in the resistor: I=U_eff/R=75/100=0.75 A. Final answer: 0.75 A.
